record.paper_title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let G be a polycyclic group. Given elements a and b in G, with the promise that there exist an integer n in N and an element g in G such that a^n = b^g, determine the computational complexity of finding such an exponent n and conjugating element g. This is the power conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups.

evidence.quote: The key exchange presented in Section 3.3.2 makes use of the power conjugacy search problem, where if it is known for some a, b ∈ G and n ∈ N that an = bg for some g ∈ G, the task is to find one such n and g.
(3) What is the complexity of the power conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series $G = G_0 \trianglerighteq G_1 \trianglerighteq \cdots \trianglerighteq G_k = \{1\}$ in which every quotient $G_i/G_{i+1}$ is cyclic. For elements $a, b \in G$ and $g \in G$, write $b^g := g^{-1} b g$.

The power conjugacy search problem in a polycyclic group $G$ is the following. Given $a, b \in G$ with the promise that there exist a positive integer $n$ and an element $g \in G$ such that
$$a^n = b^g,$$
produce such a pair $(n, g)$.

Determine the computational complexity of this problem for polycyclic groups: provide either an algorithm with a proven worst-case complexity bound, or a hardness reduction characterizing its difficulty, in the class of all (finitely presented) polycyclic groups.
artifact.status_search_result: The precise computational complexity of the power conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups appears to remain open. While the related (ordinary) conjugacy search problem has been shown to be NP-complete on certain families of polycyclic groups (Cavallo–Kahrobaei), and reductions to discrete-log-type problems are known in restricted two-generator cases, no general complexity classification of the power conjugacy search variant in arbitrary polycyclic groups was found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: A family of polycyclic groups over which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Polycyclic groups are constructed whose conjugacy search and decision problems are at least as hard as subset sum, hence NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: Conjugacy (not specifically power conjugacy) is NP-complete on some polycyclic families; general complexity of power conjugacy is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Group-based Cryptography in the Quantum Era
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys algorithmic problems in polycyclic groups used in cryptography, including conjugacy and power conjugacy search, noting their complexity in polycyclic groups is not fully understood.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey treats power conjugacy in polycyclic groups as an algorithmic problem of cryptographic interest without a definitive complexity classification.
